CHAPTER 1.1 · LEARNING AREA 1 · AUGUST · SEPTEMBER

Growth and exponential functions

A piggy bank fills up week by week by the same amount, a culture of bacteria grows hour by hour by the same factor, a cold drink approaches room temperature without ever exceeding it. You learn to tell such processes apart, to describe them recursively and explicitly, and to approximate measured data by an exponential function.

12 LESSONS3 UNITS3 LABSSUSTAINABILITY
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • tell linear, exponential, bounded and logistic growth apart from tables and graphs
  • describe processes of growth and decay recursively and explicitly, find the growth factor and interpret it
  • calculate with half-life and doubling time
  • describe the effect of the parameters in $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ and approximate measured data with an exponential regression

Calculate $1.05 \cdot 200$.

$210$, that is $200$ plus $5\%$.

A jumper costing €80 is reduced by 25%. What does it cost then?

$80 \cdot 0.75 = 60$ €

Calculate $2^5$.

$2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 32$

By which factor do you multiply for an increase of 4%?

$100\% + 4\% = 104\% = 1.04$

You put one grain of wheat on the first square of a chessboard, and on every further square twice as many as on the one before.

  • One grain weighs about 0.05 g. After how many squares is there a tonne on the board altogether?

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Processes of growth and decay

Series A from the exploration grows by 4 at each step, series B is doubled at each step. In C the increase gets smaller and smaller: 5, then 2.5, then 1.25. The distance to 20 is halved each time, and the values get closer and closer to 20. D are the square numbers; neither the differences nor the quotients are constant.

Many processes can be described step by step: the new stock $B_{n+1}$ arises from the old stock $B_n$. The way how it arises determines the growth model.

KEY POINT · GROWTH MODELS

Linear: $B_{n+1} = B_n + d$. At each step the same amount is added; the differences are constant.

Exponential: $B_{n+1} = q \cdot B_n$. At each step you multiply by the same factor; the quotients are constant. $q > 1$ means growth, $0 < q < 1$ decay. For an increase of $p\%$, $q = 1 + \tfrac{p}{100}$, for a decrease of $p\%$, $q = 1 - \tfrac{p}{100}$.

Bounded: $B_{n+1} = B_n + k \cdot (S - B_n)$. The distance to the bound $S$ shrinks at each step by the fraction $k$.

Logistic: $B_{n+1} = B_n + k \cdot B_n \cdot (S - B_n)$. Almost exponential at first, then slowed down by the bound.

In the exponential model the doubling time (for growth) and the half-life (for decay) are always the same length, no matter when you start.

Quick test: if the differences are equal, the growth is linear. If the quotients are equal, it is exponential.

Unbounded or bounded? Linear and exponential growth go beyond every limit. In nature almost every kind of growth comes up against a limit at some point: space, food, buyers.

INTERACTIVE · FOUR GROWTH MODELS

Choose a model and change the initial stock, the parameter and the bound. The points are the stocks after each step.

EXAMPLE 1 · RECOGNISING THE MODEL

A stock is measured every hour: 400, 340, 289, 245.65. Which model fits? How large is the stock after the next hour?

Differences: $-60$, $-51$, $-43.35$, not constant. Quotients: $\tfrac{340}{400} = \tfrac{289}{340} = \tfrac{245.65}{289} = 0.85$.

Exponential decrease by 15% per hour, so $245.65 \cdot 0.85 \approx 208.80$.

EXAMPLE 2 · BOUNDED GROWTH

A drink comes out of the fridge at 6 °C, and the room is at 22 °C. Every minute the distance to room temperature shrinks by 15%. How warm is it after 1, 2 and 10 minutes?

$B_1 = 6 + 0.15 \cdot (22 - 6) = 8.4$, $\;B_2 = 8.4 + 0.15 \cdot 13.6 = 10.44$.

The distance $16$ is multiplied by $0.85$ every minute: $B_n = 22 - 16 \cdot 0.85^n$, so $B_{10} \approx 18.85$ °C.

EXERCISES

Linear, exponential or neither? a) 5, 8, 11, 14   b) 2, 6, 18, 54   c) 100, 90, 81, 72.9   d) 1, 4, 9, 16

a) linear, $d = 3$   b) exponential, $q = 3$   c) exponential, $q = 0.9$   d) neither: square numbers

800 bacteria multiply by 25% per hour. How many are there after one, two and three hours?

$q = 1.25$: 1000, 1250 and 1562.5, so about 1563 bacteria.

Iodine-131 has a half-life of 8 days. How much of 120 mg is left after 8, 16, 24 and 40 days?

40 days are five half-lives.

60 mg, 30 mg, 15 mg and $120 \cdot 0.5^5 = 3.75$ mg.

A lake has room for at most 1000 fish. 200 are released into it, and every year the distance to the bound shrinks by 20%. Calculate the stock after one and two years and give an explicit formula. How many fish are there after five years?

$B_1 = 200 + 0.2 \cdot 800 = 360$, $\;B_2 = 360 + 0.2 \cdot 640 = 488$. $\;B_n = 1000 - 800 \cdot 0.8^n$, $\;B_5 \approx 738$ fish.

A water lily doubles its area every day, and after 30 days the pond is completely covered. When was it half covered, when a quarter? Roughly when was only 1% covered?

Half on day 29, a quarter on day 28. On day 23 it is $2^{-7} \approx 0.8\%$, on day 24 $2^{-6} \approx 1.6\%$: between day 23 and 24. So from 1% to full takes less than 7 days.

TEST YOURSELF!

What is the growth factor of the sequence 2, 6, 18, 54?

$\tfrac62 = \tfrac{18}{6} = 3$

A stock of 500 decreases by 10% per step. How large is it after one step?

$500 \cdot 0.9 = 450$

The distance to a limit is halved at each step. Which model is this?

Bounded growth with $k = 0.5$.

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Exponential functions and growth

On the chessboard, recursively, $a_1 = 1$ and $a_{n+1} = 2 \cdot a_n$. To know the 64th square, you would have to double 63 times. It is quicker explicitly: on square $n$ there are $a_n = 2^{n-1}$ grains, so on the 64th $2^{63} \approx 9.2 \cdot 10^{18}$.

The explicit formula is a function of time: the exponent is the variable. Such functions are called exponential functions.

KEY POINT · EXPONENTIAL GROWTH

A function $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ with $a \neq 0$, $b > 0$ and $b \neq 1$ is called an exponential function.

Exponential growth: recursively $B_{n+1} = q \cdot B_n$ with initial value $B_0$ · explicitly $B(t) = B_0 \cdot q^t$

You get the growth factor from two consecutive values, $q = \tfrac{B(t + 1)}{B(t)}$, or over $n$ steps: $q = \sqrt[n]{\tfrac{B_n}{B_0}}$.

Careful: 3% per year is not 30% after ten years, but $1.03^{10} \approx 1.344$, so a good 34%. The increases themselves earn interest too.

Recursive or explicit? Recursive is ideal for a spreadsheet (=B2*1.03), explicit for a single value far in the future.

INTERACTIVE · LINEAR VERSUS EXPONENTIAL

At the start the line is often ahead. Extend the time span and watch who wins in the end.

EXAMPLE 3 · SETTING UP THE EXPLICIT FORMULA

A town has 48,000 inhabitants and grows by 1.5% per year. How many are there after 10 years? When has the number doubled?

$E(t) = 48{,}000 \cdot 1.015^t$, so $E(10) \approx 55{,}706$.

Trying out: $1.015^{46} \approx 1.98$ and $1.015^{47} \approx 2.01$. Doubled after about 47 years. In chapter 4.2 you can do this without trying out.

EXAMPLE 4 · THE FACTOR FROM TWO VALUES

With compound interest, savings grow in 5 years from €2000 to €2433.31. What is the interest rate?

$q^5 = \tfrac{2433.31}{2000} \approx 1.2167$, so $q = \sqrt[5]{1.2167} \approx 1.04$.

The interest rate is 4% per year.

EXERCISES

Give the growth factor: a) +7%   b) −12%   c) +100%   d) −0.5%

a) $1.07$   b) $0.88$   c) $2$   d) $0.995$

Write explicitly and calculate $B_4$: a) $B_0 = 50$, $B_{n+1} = 1.2 \cdot B_n$   b) $B_0 = 3000$, $B_{n+1} = 0.75 \cdot B_n$

a) $B_n = 50 \cdot 1.2^n$, $B_4 = 103.68$   b) $B_n = 3000 \cdot 0.75^n$, $B_4 \approx 949.22$

Chessboard: how many grains are there on the 10th and on the 20th square? How many are there on the whole board?

$1 + 2 + 4 + \ldots + 2^{63}$ is 1 less than the next power of two.

$2^9 = 512$, $2^{19} = 524{,}288$. Altogether $2^{64} - 1 \approx 1.8 \cdot 10^{19}$ grains; at 0.05 g per grain, almost 1000 billion tonnes.

A smartphone costing €900 loses 30% of its value every year. What is it worth after 3 years? After how many years is it worth less than €100?

$900 \cdot 0.7^3 = 308.70$ €. $900 \cdot 0.7^6 \approx 105.88$ € and $900 \cdot 0.7^7 \approx 74.12$ €: after 7 years.

Global development: in 1960 about 3.0 billion people lived on Earth, in 2020 about 7.8 billion. Find the average annual growth factor. What would the same growth give for 2050?

$q = \sqrt[60]{\tfrac{7.8}{3.0}} \approx 1.016$, so about 1.6% per year. $7.8 \cdot 1.016^{30} \approx 12.6$ billion. The United Nations expect about 9.7 billion for 2050 (World Population Prospects 2022), because birth rates are falling: the growth has long stopped being exponential.

TEST YOURSELF!

Which factor belongs to a decrease of 12%?

$1 - 0.12 = 0.88$

$B(t) = 50 \cdot 1.2^t$. Calculate $B(2)$.

$50 \cdot 1.44 = 72$

$B_0 = 3000$ and $B_{n+1} = 0.75 \cdot B_n$. Which explicit formula is right?

The initial value is in front of the power, the factor is the base.

UNIT 3WITH AIDS · 4 LESSONS

3Parameters and regression

For the tea from the exploration, the temperature falls quickly at first and slowly later. The difference from the room temperature of 20 °C, on the other hand, shrinks every 5 minutes by almost the same factor, about $0.77$. That is exponential decay, and a regression gives the matching function.

KEY POINT · THE PARAMETERS OF f(x) = a · bx

$a = f(0)$ is the initial value; the graph cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, a)$. $b$ is the factor per step: $b > 1$ increasing, $0 < b < 1$ decreasing.

The $x$-axis is a horizontal asymptote. For $f(x) = a \cdot b^x + c$ it is the line $y = c$. The graphs of $b^x$ and $\left(\tfrac1b\right)^x$ are mirror images in the $y$-axis.

Through two points $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$: $b^{x_2 - x_1} = \tfrac{y_2}{y_1}$, then $a = \tfrac{y_1}{b^{x_1}}$.

Exponential regression with a graphing calculator or CAS: it finds $a$ and $b$ so that the curve fits all the measured values as well as possible. Check first: are the quotients roughly constant?

Limits of the model: a regression describes the measured values. Far beyond the measured values (extrapolation) it can be completely wrong.

INTERACTIVE · REGRESSION

Choose “Cooling” or “World population” and compare the models. You can move the measured points.

EXAMPLE 5 · THROUGH TWO POINTS

The graph of $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ passes through $P(1, 6)$ and $Q(3, 24)$. Find $a$ and $b$.

$\tfrac{a \cdot b^3}{a \cdot b^1} = b^2 = \tfrac{24}{6} = 4$, so $b = 2$ (the base is positive). $a = \tfrac{6}{2} = 3$.

$f(x) = 3 \cdot 2^x$

EXAMPLE 6 · TEA WITH THE GRAPHING CALCULATOR

Difference from room temperature (20 °C) every 5 minutes: 70, 55, 42, 33, 25, 19, 15 degrees. When is the tea at 60 °C?

Exponential regression: $\Delta T(t) \approx 70.7 \cdot 0.949^t$, so $T(t) \approx 20 + 70.7 \cdot 0.949^t$.

60 °C means $\Delta T = 40$. By trying out or from the graph: after about 11 minutes.

EXERCISES

Give the point of intersection with the $y$-axis and the asymptote. Does the graph rise or fall? a) $2^x$   b) $0.5^x$   c) $3 \cdot 2^x$   d) $2^x - 1$

a) $(0, 1)$, $y = 0$, rises   b) $(0, 1)$, $y = 0$, falls   c) $(0, 3)$, $y = 0$, rises   d) $(0, 0)$, $y = -1$, rises

An exponential graph passes through $(0, 5)$ and $(1, 15)$. What is the function?

$a = 5$, $b = \tfrac{15}{5} = 3$: $f(x) = 5 \cdot 3^x$

Find $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ through a) $(2, 12)$ and $(4, 48)$   b) $(1, 80)$ and $(3, 20)$.

a) $b^2 = 4$, $b = 2$, $a = \tfrac{12}{4} = 3$: $f(x) = 3 \cdot 2^x$   b) $b^2 = \tfrac14$, $b = 0.5$, $a = 160$: $f(x) = 160 \cdot 0.5^x$

In its first months an app has 12, 18, 27, 41, 61 and 91 thousand users. Use quotients to check whether exponential growth fits, and use the graphing calculator to find a regression function.

Quotients: $1.5$, $1.5$, $1.52$, $1.49$, $1.49$, almost constant. Regression: $f(t) \approx 12.0 \cdot 1.50^t$ (months from the start, thousands).

The exponential regression of the world population from 1950 to 2020 (in the widget: “World population”) predicts about 13.7 billion for 2050. Compare this with the United Nations forecast of about 9.7 billion and give reasons for the difference.

The regression continues the growth of about 1.7% per year unchanged. In fact the growth rate has been falling since the 1960s (fewer children per woman). In the long run a bounded or logistic model fits better. Extrapolation is risky.

TEST YOURSELF!

$f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ passes through $(0, 5)$ and $(1, 15)$. What is $b$?

$b = \tfrac{15}{5} = 3$

Calculate $f(3)$ for $f(x) = 160 \cdot 0.5^x$.

$160 \cdot \tfrac18 = 20$

Which horizontal asymptote does $f(x) = 2^x + 3$ have?

The whole graph is shifted up by 3.

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years. What percentage of the original C-14 is still there after 11,460 and after 17,190 years?

Two half-lives: 25%. Three half-lives: 12.5%.

Connecting with Year 9: use the laws of powers to show that $0.5^x = 2^{-x}$. What follows for the graphs of $2^x$ and $0.5^x$?

$0.5^x = \left(2^{-1}\right)^x = 2^{-x}$. The graph of $0.5^x$ arises from that of $2^x$ if you replace $x$ by $-x$: a reflection in the $y$-axis.

A new mobile game can reach at most 20,000 people in Altea, a small town in Spain. At the start nobody plays it, and every week 30% of those still missing join. Calculate the first three weeks. After how many weeks do at least 90% play?

6000, 10,200, 13,140. $B_n = 20{,}000 - 20{,}000 \cdot 0.7^n$. 90% means $0.7^n \leq 0.1$: $0.7^6 \approx 0.118$, $0.7^7 \approx 0.082$, so after 7 weeks.

A rumour at a school with 800 students: at the start 10 know it, logistic model with $k = 0.0008$. Make a table (spreadsheet: =B2+0.0008*B2*(800-B2)). From which day on do more than half know it?

16.32 · 26.55 · 42.98 · 69.01 · 109.37 · 169.79 · 255.40 · 366.67 · 493.78 … On day 9 it is about 494, so more than 400. After that the number grows more and more slowly towards 800.

EXCURSIONSUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT

The limits to growth

In 1972 a report commissioned by the Club of Rome appeared that was discussed all over the world: “The Limits to Growth”. A team around Donella and Dennis Meadows at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology had used a computer model to work out how population, industrial production, food, raw materials and pollution grow together.

The core message is mathematics: exponential growth in a limited world comes up against a limit, and it does so suddenly. The book explains this with the water lily from exercise 5: if you wait until half the pond is covered, you have only a single day left. Whether the growth then turns gently into bounded growth or overshoots the limit and collapses depends on how early you take countermeasures.

Source: Donella H. Meadows, Dennis L. Meadows, Jørgen Randers, William W. Behrens III: “The Limits to Growth”, Universe Books, New York 1972. German: “Die Grenzen des Wachstums. Bericht des Club of Rome zur Lage der Menschheit”, Deutsche Verlags-Anstalt, Stuttgart 1972.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

LINEAR AND EXPONENTIAL

Linear: equal differences, $B_{n+1} = B_n + d$. Exponential: equal quotients, $B_{n+1} = q \cdot B_n$.

5, 8, 11, 14: $d = 3$ · 2, 6, 18, 54: $q = 3$

BOUNDED AND LOGISTIC

The distance to the bound $S$ shrinks: $B_{n+1} = B_n + k(S - B_n)$. Logistic: $B_{n+1} = B_n + k B_n (S - B_n)$.

$B_n = 22 - 16 \cdot 0.85^n$: the drink approaches 22 °C

EXPLICIT

$B(t) = B_0 \cdot q^t$ with $q = 1 \pm \tfrac{p}{100}$. Half-life and doubling time are constant.

$48{,}000 \cdot 1.015^{10} \approx 55{,}706$

PARAMETERS

$f(x) = a \cdot b^x$: $a = f(0)$, $b$ the factor per step, asymptote $y = 0$ (with $+ c$: $y = c$).

through $(1, 6)$ and $(3, 24)$: $f(x) = 3 \cdot 2^x$

REGRESSION

Check the quotients first, then fit with the graphing calculator. Be careful when extrapolating.

Tea: $\Delta T(t) \approx 70.7 \cdot 0.949^t$
